# Implementation Plan: User Authentication System

**Branch**: `001-add-jwt-auth` | **Date**: 2026-05-09 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-user-auth-system/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan is generated by the `/speckit.plan` command and follows the workflow in `.specify/templates/plan-template.md`.

## Summary

Implement a secure user authentication system with registration (email/password), login with JWT tokens backed by server-side session records, password reset via email (15-minute tokens), and 24-hour session expiry with revocation support. All credentials use bcrypt hashing, passwords enforce 12-char complexity (upper/lowercase/number/symbol), and failed logins trigger progressive lockout (5 failures → 15-min lock, escalating). Reset emails retry up to 3 times with generic success responses to prevent account enumeration. The auth system targets Express.js/TypeScript on Node.js with PostgreSQL persistence, Jest unit/integration tests at 80%+ business-logic coverage, and JSDoc-documented public APIs. Core user stories deliver independently: registration & sign-in (P1), password recovery (P2), session management (P3).

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5.x (Node.js 18+)  
**Primary Dependencies**: Express.js 4.x, jsonwebtoken (JWT issuance/validation), bcrypt (password hashing), nodemailer (email delivery), pg (PostgreSQL client)  
**Storage**: PostgreSQL 14+ with schema for users, sessions (with jti), reset_requests, and auth_events tables.  
**Testing**: Jest 29+ with ts-jest; unit tests for crypto, token logic, and email retry logic; integration tests for full auth flows and edge cases.  
**Target Platform**: Linux server (Debian/Ubuntu preferred); Node.js 18+ LTS runtime.
**Project Type**: web-service (backend API; frontend out of scope for v1)  
**Performance Goals**: <100ms p95 for register/login endpoints; <200ms for password reset; session revocation checks <50ms.  
**Constraints**: All credentials hashed with bcrypt (salt rounds ≥10); no plaintext secrets in code; all auth events logged with correlation IDs; JWT refresh/revocation checked per-request.  
**Scale/Scope**: Target 10,000 concurrent active users in v1; 3 user stories; brownfield integration with existing protected features expecting JWT Bearer tokens.

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

**GATE PASS**: All constitutional principles satisfied at planning entry.

- ✅ **Clean Code First**: Module boundaries defined: `src/models/` (User, Session, ResetRequest entities), `src/services/` (auth, email, crypto, session lifecycle), `src/routes/` (endpoint definitions), `src/middleware/` (JWT validation). Naming conventions enforce explicitness (e.g., `validatePasswordPolicy()`, `issueJWT()`). No cross-cutting duplication; shared utilities in `src/lib/crypto.ts`, `src/lib/email.ts`.
- ✅ **TypeScript Strict Mode**: Confirmed TypeScript 5.x with `strict: true` in tsconfig.json; no `any` types permitted except explicit eslint exceptions with documented rationale. All Express route handlers, middleware, and service methods typed.
- ✅ **Testing Pyramid + Coverage**: Unit tests target crypto (bcrypt, JWT), validation logic, email retry queuing (~40 test cases, expected 85%+ coverage). Integration tests cover user journeys and edge cases (duplicate registration, concurrent password reset, token revocation after reset) (~20 test cases, 15%+ coverage). E2E tests deferred to acceptance validation post-merge.
- ✅ **JSDoc Requirement**: All service exports (AuthService, SessionManager, PasswordResetService, etc.) documented with parameter/return types, error contracts, and side effects. Middleware and utility functions similarly documented.
- ✅ **Change Size Control**: Feature decomposed into 3 independent user stories (P1/P2/P3) per spec; tasks separated by concern (models, services, routes, tests, documentation). Checkpoints after each story enable incremental validation.

**Structure Decision**: Single project layout for backend web-service. All auth logic centralized in `src/services/` with model entities in `src/models/`. Express routes in `src/routes/` follow REST conventions. Middleware stack in `src/middleware/` enforces JWT validation on protected routes. Database connection and configuration isolated in `src/lib/` for testability. Unit tests target business logic; integration tests cover full user journeys. Database migrations version schema incrementally.
